text: Nine oh four in the morning. An exam paper is already on WhatsApp, an hour before the exam. Five hundred colleges printed it. Which one leaked it?
sub: 9:04 in the morning. An exam paper is already on WhatsApp, an hour before the exam. 500 colleges printed it. Which one leaked it?

text: Leak Trace gives every college the same questions and the same marks. But each copy hides its own pattern: its own question order, and its own approved wording.
There are three layers: the order, the wording, and the numbers and answer letters. A leaker can't change that last layer without making the leaked answers wrong.
Let's be the leaker. We retype seven questions, with typos, and no question numbers.
Leak Trace names a college only when the odds reach ten thousand to one. Here, it does.
sub: Leak Trace names a college only when the odds reach 10,000 to 1. Here, it does.

text: Each line adds evidence, until one college crosses the bar.
Now try to dodge it. Reword every line, and shuffle the order.
With the order and wording gone, it holds back instead of guessing. No innocent college is named.
Even a leaked answer key gives the college away. With coded keys, any two colleges differ in at least twelve of twenty answers.
sub: Even a leaked answer key gives the college away. With coded keys, any two colleges differ in at least 12 of 20 answers.

text: Sixteen answers, one in ten of them wrong, and the source is still named.
sub: 16 answers, one in ten of them wrong, and the source is still named.

text: Now, two hundred random leaks at once.
Innocent colleges blamed: zero. Across a hundred and forty-eight thousand attack leaks, just one, from a chance match on a copy from outside the system.
sub: Innocent colleges blamed: zero. Across 148,000 attack leaks, just one, from a chance match on a copy from outside the system.

text: And there is a proof. Under our model, a copy from outside the system clears the bar at most once in ten thousand times. We checked it on eight hundred thousand simulated copies.
sub: And there is a proof. Under our model, a copy from outside the system clears the bar at most once in 10,000 times. We checked it on 800,000 simulated copies.

text: It is all in a fifteen page research paper, with open code and data. Every result so far is simulated. Next comes a pilot in one college.
sub: It is all in a 15-page research paper, with open code and data. Every result so far is simulated. Next comes a pilot in one college.
